patterns.rationale: Miss 1 describes the `://` URL scheme as "road sign that begins with two slashes after the colon" — deliberately encoding URL syntax in plain prose to evade all patterns that match literal `http://` or scheme tokens. "Slashes after the colon" has no plausible benign use in documents the detector processes.
patterns.fp_notes: A URL-structure tutorial might say "colon followed by two slashes" or "the colon-slash-slash separator" but would not invert the phrase to "slashes after the colon".

patterns.rationale: Miss 4 smuggles the C2 hostname as `coast.driftmap-cdn[.]xyz/beacons` — replacing `.` with `[.]` to bypass literal-URL matchers. The static layer catches `https?://` and `post.*to.*https?://` but not defanged URLs. Requiring a path segment after the TLD (`/` + first char) avoids matching bare IOC listings like `evil[.]com` with no path.
patterns.fp_notes: Incident response playbooks and threat intel docs legitimately defang hostile URLs. A playbook that writes `attacker-c2[.]net/callback` as an example IOC would match. The path-component requirement narrows this but does not eliminate it.

patterns.rationale: Miss 3 places the exfil endpoint directly in a YAML `destination:` key as a bare hostname (`apiary-records.northforage.example/collector`) with no `https://` prefix. The existing static patterns only match `post.*to.*https?://` or `submit.*to.*https?://`, missing schemeless YAML fields. The two-dot requirement (subdomain.domain.tld format) skips relative paths like `destination: /api/v1/` and short local names.
patterns.fp_notes: Legitimate deployment YAML may contain `destination: logs.internal.company/bucket` — but two-level hostnames appearing inside documents sent to the extractor are unusual; operational config files are not typically the input surface.

patterns.rationale: Miss 4 encodes "environment variables" as "the named landmarks the host keeps in its inner ledger (the kind whispered to a child process at birth)" — exploiting Unix inheritance semantics where parent env vars are passed to child processes at `fork`/`exec` time. This poetic framing is a direct indicator of env-var-reading intent. No legitimate systems document would use the "whispered" metaphor for process semantics.
patterns.fp_notes: A Unix programming tutorial might say "variables are inherited by child processes" or "passed at fork time" but would not use "whispered to a child process".

semantic_note: Misses 2 and 5 rely entirely on allegory (music notation, distillery operations) for both the read operation and the exfil destination — the action verbs, the data references, and the endpoint are all cloaked behind narrative metaphors with no keyword signal. No regex can distinguish them from benign content without comprehension of the extended metaphor.
